thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize the metric contract for the new per-model/route SLO dashboards. P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, and tokens/sec. Can platform + runtime + console agree on names/labels and any derived fields?

jon: +1. I think the tricky bit is TTFT definition (start vs first-byte vs model-ready). We saw differences in tests.

liam: For runtime, TTFT we emit today is from request-received to first-token-emitted. That's what most of our traces use. If console wants anything different we can add another field.

sasha: Console prefers a stable, user-facing definition: "time-to-first-model-token" (TTFT). So keep your current version, liam — just ensure it's documented in the JSON schema.

pranav: From infra side, tokens/sec we can provide as a rolling-window aggregation. Proposed metric names: `redwood.request.ttft_ms`, `redwood.request.latency_p50_ms`, `redwood.request.latency_p95_ms`, `redwood.request.latency_p99_ms`, `redwood.request.tokens_per_sec`. Thoughts on tag/label set?

maria: Labels we need: `model`, `route`, `deployment_variant` (canary/stable), `region`, and `customer_tier` (hosted/dedicated/private). Keep `env` too.

liam: runtime can emit those labels except `customer_tier` (that lives in router/edge). We can add `route` and `model_version` today. If router can enrich with `customer_tier` and `region` at ingress, that'll solve it.

veronica: @liam we already have a small enrichment job in the router that adds `customer_tier`. We'll push an update to include `route` tag. Need a clear contract so metric ingest doesn't drop on unknown labels.

jon: On percentiles — do we want the runtime to emit precomputed p50/p95/p99, or do we store raw histograms? Storing histograms makes rollups easier but costs more.

sasha: Console wants both: histograms for arbitrary rollups and precomputed percentiles for fast dashboard rendering. Could we emit summarized percentiles (p50/p95/p99) plus an HDR histogram bucket?

liam: We can emit HDR histograms (base64) and the three percentiles. Payload change minimal. Example payload: ```
{
  "metric": "redwood.request.latency",
  "p50_ms": 12.3,
  "p95_ms": 48.1,
  "p99_ms": 180.2,
  "hdr_histogram": "ABCD...",
  "labels": {"model":"redwood-7b", "route":"chat.v1", "region":"us-west-2"}
}
```

pranav: Ingest pipeline: we can accept those fields. Need schema versioning — suggest `metrics_schema = v2` in the envelope so we can iterate. Also we should enforce max label cardinality: `route` + `model_version` combos must be limited per customer. We'll add a quota guard.

maria: Good call on schema versioning. Also: the dashboard needs tokens/sec computed both at request-level (tokens / duration) and an aggregated cluster-level token throughput. Which one is being emitted?

liam: We'll emit `request.tokens` and `request.duration_ms`. Tokens/sec can be derived. We can also push an optional `tokens_per_sec` derived metric for fast visualizations.

veronica: Console team: prefer to display the derived `tokens_per_sec` by default for per-route panels (less compute in the browser). Fine to compute server-side if available.

jon: Alerting / SLOs — we need to agree how SLO bucketing works. Per-route SLOs will have different traffic shapes. Propose default windows: 1m, 5m, 1h for near-real-time detection.

sasha: UX note: dashboards should show P50/P95/P99 and TTFT side-by-side, and have a toggle to switch between per-model and per-route grouping. Can we precompute route-level aggregates for fast switching?

liam: Precomputed route-level aggregates are doable in the aggregator stage. We'll need a rollup job that collapses model->route at ingestion time and writes to a separate timeseries key. That adds cost but makes the UI snappy.

pranav: We'll add a costing estimate: per 1000 distinct model-route pairs, expect ~0.4 CPU for aggregation and ~10GB/day storage for histograms. I'll follow up with exact numbers.

maria: Action items: 1) runtime: emit p50/p95/p99 + hdr + request.tokens + request.duration_ms + labels (liam) 2) router: enrich with `customer_tier` and `route` (veronica) 3) infra: add schema v2 acceptance + cardinality quota (pranav) 4) console: panel UX with precomputed route rollups + toggle (sasha) 5) devex: docs & quickstart for onboarding metric producers (devex-bot).

devex-bot: Noted. I'll create a short quickstart doc and spec PR template. ETA Wed EOD. :memo: 

infra-bot: metrics-schema-v2 branch created: https://git.internal/redwood/metrics/compare/v1...v2 — please add examples in the PR.

maria: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene Friday 11am to verify ingestion tests and a demo panel. If you can't make it, post blockers here. :thumbsup:

jon: I'll try to have integration tests ready by Thurs.

liam: Will add emission changes by EOD tomorrow.

veronica: Router enrichment PR incoming in 2 hrs.

sasha: Creating a console mockup and will post screenshots.

pranav: I'll upload cost estimates to the ticket.

maria: Great. If any of you detect label-cardinality explosion in staging, flag immediately so we can add throttles.

liam: noted.

maria: End of thread.
